comments.note: gui/config.ts placed in src/gui/config.ts (not mcp-server/gui/config.ts as specified in the WP) to comply with tsconfig rootDir: './src' and include: ['src/**/*'] constraints. The gui/ directory at mcp-server root is still the correct location for the HTTP server files (WP-002+) which will be a separate process with their own build config.

getMaxHandoffDepth() try/catch is technically redundant since _cache is always initialized to DEFAULT_CONFIG and getConfig() never throws. However, the safety net is cheap and useful as a defense against future refactoring.

The auto_handoff_enabled check was added to the if-condition in buildHandoffResponse() before isRegistryLoaded(). The short-circuit prevents any registry/storage access when handoffs are disabled — correct behavior.

comments.note: No unit tests for gui/config.ts module directly (readConfigFromDisk with valid file, readConfigFromDisk ENOENT self-heal, writeConfig atomic write, startConfigWatcher/stopConfigWatcher). The acceptance criteria are satisfied via integration and behavior tests, but a dedicated test file for src/gui/config.ts would improve coverage and regression detection.

startConfigWatcher() uses { persistent: false } on the FSWatcher so the watcher does not prevent Node.js from exiting. This is correct for production use but means watcher tests must be carefully timed — not currently tested with actual file-write simulation.

summary: No circular dependencies in import graph for gui/config.ts
Condition ordering in buildHandoffResponse() is optimal (status guards → config check → registry check)
Module-level singleton pattern is correct for ESM module caching
All file writes use atomicWriteJson(); all logging uses process.stderr.write()
ESM .js extensions used on all local imports
Code is clean, idiomatic TypeScript, and maintainable

comments.note: src/gui/config.ts has no circular dependency risks: it only imports from fs, zod, and storage/atomic-writer.ts. The dependency graph is clean.

Auto-handoff eligibility condition ordering in buildHandoffResponse() is optimal: cheap status guards precede config check (in-memory), which precedes registry check. The auto_handoff_enabled flag short-circuits before any I/O-adjacent checks.

Module-level singleton approach in gui/config.ts is consistent with Node.js ESM module caching. readConfigFromDisk() is async for atomic write self-healing; getConfig() remains synchronous and zero-cost for the hot path.
